$comment: Rule catalog — data. Standards 5 through 8: freshness, missing information, sample-size sufficiency, and outliers. Carries two prohibitions: using stale information without accounting for it, and ignoring missing critical information.

rules.title: The record states when its data was current
rules.description: The record states the instant its underlying data describes, and the window within which that data stays usable.
rules.rationale: Staleness cannot be assessed without a date. The instant the data describes is not the instant it was fetched, and using the fetch time hides exactly the gap that matters.
rules.remediation: Record data.freshness.dataAsOf, and a freshnessWindow when the project default does not fit this prediction.

rules.title: Stale information is never used as though it were current
rules.description: Where the data is older than its freshness window at the time the prediction was generated, the record states how that age was allowed for.
rules.rationale: Using old data is often unavoidable and sometimes fine. Using it without widening the interval, decaying its weight, or otherwise acknowledging its age produces a prediction that is confident about a world that has moved on.
rules.remediation: State how staleness was handled in data.freshness.stalenessAccounted, or refresh the inputs.
rules.$assuranceNote: The evaluator establishes that an accounting was WRITTEN when the data was past its window. It cannot establish that the accounting was adequate, or that the declared window was honest.

rules.title: Known gaps in the evidence are stated
rules.description: The record lists what is known to be missing, separating gaps judged immaterial from information judged critical.
rules.rationale: An empty list of gaps is a claim that someone looked. Silence is not, and the two are indistinguishable to a reader unless the record makes the distinction itself.
rules.remediation: Populate data.completeness.knownGaps and criticalMissing, using empty arrays deliberately rather than by omission.
rules.$assuranceNote: The evaluator sees the gaps that were declared. Information nobody realised was missing is by its nature absent from this list, and no structural check can find it.

rules.title: Missing critical information is never ignored
rules.description: Where information judged critical is missing, a prediction either justifies why it is defensible anyway, or gives way to an abstention.
rules.rationale: The record itself has already said this information bears materially on the outcome. Predicting anyway without saying why is the point at which a system starts manufacturing certainty it does not have.
rules.remediation: Write data.completeness.justification, or replace the prediction with an abstention citing missing-critical-information.
rules.$assuranceNote: This rule acts on what the record admits is critical. A record that quietly classifies decisive information as an immaterial gap passes it, which is why the classification itself belongs under human review.

rules.title: The sample behind the prediction is stated
rules.description: The record states how many observations support the prediction, what each observation is, and why those are the relevant ones.
rules.rationale: A bare count is uninterpretable and a missing one hides everything. The unit matters as much as the number: 500 minutes and 500 seasons are not comparable evidence.
rules.remediation: Record data.sampleSize with n, unit, and basis.

rules.title: The sample is large enough for the claim, or the shortfall is justified
rules.description: The sample meets the project's declared minimum, or the record explains why a smaller one suffices here.
rules.rationale: Below some size a rate estimate is dominated by noise, and the resulting probability describes the sample rather than the world. The threshold is a project judgement, which is why it lives in policy rather than here.
rules.remediation: Gather more observations, justify the shortfall in data.sampleSize.justification, or abstain.
rules.$assuranceNote: This compares a count against a policy threshold. Sufficiency actually depends on effect size, base rate, and the structure of the data, none of which a count captures; a passing record is one that cleared a crude bar, not one shown to have enough evidence.

rules.title: Outliers are assessed, and their treatment is stated
rules.description: The record states that outliers were looked for, and where any were found, what was done with them.
rules.rationale: Extreme observations are either the most informative points in the sample or contamination, and which one they are is a judgement. Removing them silently is the difference between cleaning data and shaping a result.
rules.remediation: Set data.outliers.assessed, and describe handling whenever outliers were detected.
rules.$assuranceNote: The evaluator establishes that an assessment was declared and that detected outliers were said to be handled somehow. Whether the handling was principled or convenient is not observable here.
